head.title: Who's buying, who won, what moved
head.sub: 29 Sept – 5 Oct 2026 · 115 new projects in 58 countries · 37 tenders · 57 awards · 276 trade-flow signals

editor:
This week
Europe did the buying this week. Tenders rose from 6 to 37 on the week, nearly all of them public notices from Poland, the UK, Ireland and the Balkans, and the biggest award was Romania's US$2.2bn Cernavodă nuclear contract, which went to a Canadian-Italian-Korean consortium; the five largest awards went to Canadian, Irish, British and Indian contractors. If you sell into European power and rail, the bid calendar below is your next fortnight; if you buy, the award values are your benchmarks. On the water, Hormuz crude is back to pre-war volumes while Venezuela's barrels are being priced out by freight.
— Yi Huang, World Trade Pro

Nuclear Power Station Construction Work at CNE Cernavodă
Awarded  ·  🇷🇴 Romania  ·  US$2.2bn  ·  won by Candu Energy, Canadian Commercial Corporation, Ansaldo Nucleare, Korea
A US$2.2bn civil package for two CANDU units sets the European nuclear benchmark this year; the consortium will now place heavy civil, M&E and site-services subcontracts in Romania.
calls.call: The call: Candu Energy, Canadian Commercial Corporation, Ansaldo Nucleare, Korea is now buying equipment and placing subcontracts. Get on their vendor list.
calls.buyer: For buyers: Reference price: US$2.2bn for this scope in Romania. Candu Energy, Canadian Commercial Corporation, Ansaldo Nucleare, Korea is now booked on this job.

The MaresConnect 750MW HVDC Interconnector System
Tender  ·  🇮🇪 Ireland  ·  US$1.1bn  ·  buyer MaresConnect Limited (MCL)

items.title: Venezuela’s Oil Exports Drop 9% as Freight Costs Bite
items.summary: Venezuela’s oil exports fell nearly 9% in September to 1.08 million barrels per day as soaring tanker costs forced traders to demand steeper…
items.html:
Oil, gas & LNG
🇻🇪 Venezuela’s Oil Exports Drop 9% as Freight Costs Bite
oilprice.com
Venezuela’s oil exports fell nearly 9% in September to 1.08 million barrels per day as soaring tanker costs forced traders to demand steeper…
What it means: Freight, not supply, is cutting Venezuelan exports: buyers of heavy sour crude get steeper discounts but fewer and later cargoes.

items.title: New limits: More ships can transit this key cargo chokepoint
items.summary: The Panama Canal has raised the number of daily transit slots for the largest container vessels.
items.html:
Shipping, ports & logistics  Panama Canal
🇵🇦 New limits: More ships can transit this key cargo chokepoint
freightwaves.com
The Panama Canal has raised the number of daily transit slots for the largest container vessels.
What it means: More daily slots for the largest ships means shorter queues on the US Gulf to Asia route; LNG and grain shippers should see slot premiums ease.

items.title: Middle East Oil Exports Stage a Remarkable Comeback
items.summary: Exports of crude oil from the Middle East hit their highest level in September since the war with Iran began, reinforcing a trend of increased…
items.html:
Oil, gas & LNG  Strait of Hormuz
🇮🇷 Middle East Oil Exports Stage a Remarkable Comeback
oilprice.com · 2 reports this week
Exports of crude oil from the Middle East hit their highest level in September since the war with Iran began, reinforcing a trend of increased…
What it means: Gulf crude is flowing at the highest level since the war began: more offers for Asian refiners, even as attacks on shipping keep war-risk premiums in freight.

items.title: Crude oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz hit prewar levels, but fuel shipments remain constrained
items.summary: Crude oil exports from the Strait of Hormuz have basically returned to levels normal before the Iran war, as U.S. military escorts have boosted…
items.html:
Shipping, ports & logistics  Strait of Hormuz
🇮🇷 Crude oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz hit prewar levels, but fuel shipments remain constrained
hellenicshippingnews.com · 6 reports this week
Crude oil exports from the Strait of Hormuz have basically returned to levels normal before the Iran war, as U.S. military escorts have boosted…
What it means: Crude through Hormuz is back to pre-war levels but refined products are not: product buyers east of Suez stay short while crude buyers are supplied.

items.title: Wheat bounces and corn manages a mostly firm finish
items.summary: Soybeans were lower on fund and technical selling.
items.html:
Agriculture & food
🇨🇳 Wheat bounces and corn manages a mostly firm finish
brownfieldagnews.com
Soybeans were lower on fund and technical selling.
What it means: Wheat and corn firmed into the week's close; importers tendering this month are buying into a bounce, not a dip.

items.title: Record cheese, butterfat exports point to strong 2026 for dairy
items.summary: 2026 could be another record year for U.S. dairy exports. CoBank ag economist Abbi Groves says international business continues to be strong.
items.html:
Agriculture & food
🇺🇸 Record cheese, butterfat exports point to strong 2026 for dairy
brownfieldagnews.com
2026 could be another record year for U.S. dairy exports. CoBank ag economist Abbi Groves says international business continues to be strong.
What it means: Record US cheese and butterfat exports mean more reefer demand on US export lanes and firmer dairy offers for importers into 2026.
